title: "In the Mood": Joe Garland, Eddie Durham and the 1936 recording
summary: Garland wrote "In the Mood"; Clarke gave it to Eddie Durham for Glenn Miller, and Hayes's band had recorded it years earlier.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And a lot of the people, like -- well, Joe Garland wrote, 'In the Mood.'
Then Eddie Durham was writing for Glenn Miller.
So he asked me, 'Hey, Kenny, any new things? Because I'm writing. I need all the music I can get.' And I brought him, 'In the Mood.'
No kidding. No kidding. How about that.
Did Joe Garland get his on it?
Oh, he's still -- he made so much money from that. Oh, we had recorded it in 1936.
Yeah, I think I do remember that you had, a year or two before Glenn Miller did it.
Before, oh, yeah, about three or four years before Glenn Miller.
